A.note: Best frame. It has a readable rock, ships, camp fires with smoke, troop blocks and varied grass and trees with believable lighting. The troops are small, uniform blocks, so they look slightly like game pieces. The foreground is a little busy and the scale is a bit unclear.

B.note: The ground is a photoreal-ish dry ochre, but it is almost one colour field. There are no troops, camps or ships, so the siege doesn't read. Faint marks and patches are the only content.

C.note: Flat, smooth, game-map terrain. The camp grids and tree dots look like tiles and are not readable as camps or troops. The rock and sea are fine but sterile.

D.note: Similar to C but flatter and paler. The camp rectangles are speckled with dots and there are no clear people, smoke or ships. The terrain is a flat colour field with a bland sky and sea.

why: A is the only frame that shows a believable siege, with ships, smoke, troops and textured terrain. B is empty but at least reads as a real landscape, while C and D are flat game-map colour fields.
top_fix_for_best: Break up the uniform troop blocks. Add varied formations, individual figures, tents and baggage, plus trenches and batteries aimed at the rock. Add depth haze and stronger foreground blur, and thin out the foreground clutter so the camp lines read clearly.
